title: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history — review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #40 (api-stocks-history), tracked here so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: An unbounded numeric `range` value (e.g. `range=999999999y`, or an arbitrarily long digit string like `range=99999999999999999999999d`) matches the route's own `_RANGE_PATTERN` (`^(max|\d+[dwmy])$`, no upper bound on digit count) but crashes `_trim_to_range`'s `pd.DateOffset` arithmetic in `backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py` with an unhandled `ValueError`/`OverflowError`, which FastAPI turns into a generic `500 Internal Server Error` instead of the `422` the endpoint's own contract promises for a bad `range`. Verified directly: `TestClient(app).get('/api/stocks/AAPL/history', params={'range': '999999999y'})` returns `500`. Fix by either bounding the pattern's digit count (e.g. `\d{1,4}`) or catching the overflow in `_trim_to_range` and mapping it to the same `422` path as a malformed `range`.

The 404 (unknown ticker) integration test only exercises the `interval=daily` path (`failing_daily`); no test exercises `interval=weekly` hitting the same `TickerNotFoundError` -> 404 mapping through `get_weekly_ohlcv`. Low risk since both branches share identical exception handling, but worth a one-line test for completeness.

decisions.decision: Fixed the range-overflow 500 with both of the task's suggested approaches, not just one: capped `_RANGE_PATTERN`'s digit run at 4 characters (`\d{1,4}`, max 9999) so FastAPI's own pattern validation rejects an absurd digit count (e.g. the 23-digit example) via the standard 422 HTTPValidationError shape before `_trim_to_range` ever runs, *and* wrapped `_trim_to_range`'s `pd.DateOffset` arithmetic in a try/except that raises a new `_RangeOutOfBoundsError` (a `ValueError` subclass), caught in `get_history` and mapped to `HTTPException(422)`.
decisions.rationale: A 4-digit cap alone isn't sufficient: '9999y' (4 digits, passes the cap) still overflows pd.Timestamp's ~1677-2262 bounds when subtracted from a real anchor date (verified directly: `pd.Timestamp('2025-01-01') - pd.DateOffset(years=9999)` raises `ValueError: year -7974 is out of range`), so the pattern fix alone (rejected as the sole fix) would leave the 'm'/'y' units still able to 500 on a value as short as 4 digits. Catching the overflow alone (rejected as the sole fix, without the pattern cap) would still let an unbounded digit string do wasted int-parsing work, and Python's int-from-string conversion has its own default 4300-digit safety limit (`sys.set_int_max_str_digits`) that a genuinely enormous digit string could hit as a plain `ValueError` before/independent of the DateOffset call anyway -- capping the pattern gives a cleaner, more standard 422 shape for that case for free, so both fixes are complementary rather than either being sufficient alone. Chose 4 digits (max 9999) as the cap rather than something tighter like 2-3 digits, since docs/Analyse.md and the existing tests never reference a range longer than a couple of years and nothing in the endpoint's contract implies a use case beyond low hundreds of days/weeks/months/years.
